answer: Topology-Distance Attenuation. Agents only accept transactions from peers whose shortest path to a trusted seed stays under a fixed hop limit. New identities attach at the transparent crystal edge of the graph, where their reachable radius is one hop. Each extra hop requires routing through existing high-degree nodes, and those nodes ration connections by local density, so a sybil cluster stays stuck at its own hollow rim. Attackers must either grow genuine long-range links or accept a lagoon of isolated leaves, costing a real edge per identity.
